subject: Sustained QPS & Latency Budget — Private GPU Pool Plan
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <ops@orchidai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sustained QPS targets for private deployment (OrchidAI)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. OrchidAI is lining up a proof-of-concept to run a private deployment in our GCP VPC and we want to make sure the sizing exercise is realistic before we commit a small pool of GPUs. High level requirements:

- Sustained inference load: 1,800 qps (mixed text generation + embeddings) with 8k token avg context for generation, 512 for embeddings.
- 99th pct latency target for generation requests: < 400ms (token-level tail is a secondary metric).
- Burst capacity to 3,500 qps for short windows (1–5 minutes) without dropping requests.
- We will run in a single region (us-west1) and require predictable egress limits.

Attached is our initial QPS requirements doc (orchidai_qps_requirements_v1.pdf). Can you outline the sizing you recommend for a private GPU pool, warmup strategies, and where network egress or KV cache limits might bite? Also interested in estimated cost and a short checklist for ops to verify connectivity.

Jordan Lee
Head of Infrastructure, OrchidAI
ops@orchidai.com

Jordan —

Appreciate the clarity; good starting point. High-level reply and plan:

Summary recommendation (short):
- Dedicated private pool: start with 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (dense inference flavor) with prewarmed KV caches and token-level batching tuned for your 8k context workloads.
- Autoscale policy: add 8-GPU steps with a 90s warmup window and a burst headroom queueing policy to absorb 1–5 minute spikes up to 3.5k qps.
- Networking: reserve 10 Gbps of egress per GPU node and validate MTU and TCP window settings; if you see >6k concurrent TLS connections, move to a connection-proxy design.

Operational notes (we'll follow up with calculations):
- Expected sustained throughput per A100-eq GPU for your mixed profile: ~120–140 qps sustained (with our batching + KV).
- With 16 GPUs: 1,920–2,240 qps sustained (fits your 1,800 qps target with modest headroom).
- Burst sizing: configure request-level admission control and a 30s fast-path cache warmup for hot prefixes to hit the 3.5k burst goal without cold-start penalties.

Next steps:
1) We'll run a short modeling spreadsheet and an internal simulation (I attached qps_modeling_v2.xlsx) to show sensitivity to batch window, average tokens per request, and cache hit ratio.
2) Rishi: can you validate the 120–140 qps/GPU number based on our recent 8k-token runbook?
3) Jordan: can you share expected concurrency profile (per-client connection counts) and egress limits so we can tune networking assumptions?

I'll loop in our network SME (Irene) on MTU/TCP tuning and the ops checklist.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Kim — quick calc from our 8k-token perf bench:

- Baseline (no KV cache, single-request batching): ~60 qps/GPU.
- With continuous batching and KV prefix caching tuned for Orchid's prompt shapes (expected 45–55% cache hit): ~130 qps/GPU median, 95th ~90 qps/GPU depending on token mix.
- Tail risks: any payloads that force full context recompute drop qps per GPU by ~25–40%.

Conservative recommendation: size for 115 qps/GPU sustained to cover tail and slightly lower cache-hit scenarios. With 16 GPUs that gives ~1,840 qps. For bursts, our admission control + queueing increases effective burst capacity by absorbing short spikes and returning larger batches to GPUs.

I'll draft a short appendix with how batch-window and cache hit % map to qps in the spreadsheet. Also flagging network: 8k context generation significantly increases packet sizes and sustained egress — assume 9–11 Gbps per node under your target qps if you serialize outputs.

-rishi

On a separate note: Irene, can you validate the 9–11 Gbps/node assumption for us?
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <ops@orchidai.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained QPS targets for private deployment (OrchidAI)

Jordan / team —

Network validation notes:
- The 9–11 Gbps/node figure is plausible if outputs average ~1.2–1.5KB per request for generation (8k context with average completion lengths). If you compress TLS payloads (HTTP/2 + gzip) you'll see ~10–20% savings.
- MTU: confirm jumbo frame support across your VPC path; enabling 9000 MTU yields measurable CPU savings on the NICs when handling many concurrent connections.
- TLS session reuse behind an ingress proxy will reduce handshake overhead; consider a connection pooler on Orchid's side.

Ops checklist (short):
- Validate VPC egress quotas with GCP network team (target: reserve 200 Gbps headroom for whole pool).
- Confirm NAT gateway scaling or use private egress appliance to keep burst egress consistent.
- Verify firewalls allow persistent long-lived connections and that idle timeouts are >300s for client keepalives.

Jordan: if you can, share a p95 of response sizes and an estimate of concurrent TCP connections per client (we'll map it in the spreadsheet).

-Irene

Thanks all — this is super helpful. Quick answers:

- We can commit to 1,900 qps sustained for the POC window and will provision for up to 4,000 qps short bursts via a temporary burst pool.
- Typical response payload p95: ~1.3KB for generation and 0.45KB for embeddings.
- Concurrent TCP connections: we expect around 2,500–3,000 concurrent clients at peak.
- Procurement will need an ops checklist and an estimated monthly cost to approve the trial. I've CC'd Procurement but they'll follow up with a PO request if numbers look sane.

Next asks for Redwood:
1) Finalized recommended node count & autoscale breakpoints (we prefer discrete commit+burst model).
2) Ops checklist suitable for our SREs (network steps, egress checks, firewall/cert items).
3) Estimated monthly cost bands for steady-state and for a 30% utilization burst scenario.

If you can get these back by EOD Friday (10/16) we can circulate internally and lock the PO.
